# SharpImage — AI Agent Usage Guide

A pure C# .NET 10 port of ImageMagick. Zero native dependencies, AOT-compatible.
This document is for AI coding agents using SharpImage as a NuGet package.

- **Package**: `Echostorm.SharpImage`
- **Target**: .NET 10.0
- **Install**: `dotnet add package Echostorm.SharpImage`
- **Repo**: https://github.com/Echostorm44/SharpImage

---

## 30-Second Quickstart

If you only read this section, you can write working code:

```csharp
using SharpImage;

// Fluent pipeline — recommended path. Auto-disposes intermediates.
ImagePipeline.Load("input.jpg")
    .Resize(800, 600)
    .Sharpen(sigma: 0.5, amount: 1.5)
    .Save("output.png")
    .Dispose();
```

That's it. The fluent `ImagePipeline` API is the recommended way to use SharpImage
for most tasks because it eliminates the manual disposal management that the
underlying static-method API requires. Read the rest of this doc only if you need
operations the pipeline doesn't expose, or if you're working with frames directly.

---

## Two API Layers

SharpImage has **two layers** that work on the same underlying types:

1. **`ImagePipeline`** (recommended) — fluent, auto-disposes intermediates.
   Top-level namespace `SharpImage`.
2. **Static classes** (advanced) — `Resize.Apply(...)`, `Geometry.Crop(...)`,
   `EnhanceOps.Modulate(...)`, etc. Each call returns a new `ImageFrame` that
   the caller is responsible for disposing.

Use the pipeline for chains. Use static classes when you need an op the
pipeline doesn't expose, when you're integrating into existing code that
manages `ImageFrame` instances, or when you need to fan one frame out to
several outputs.

---

## Namespace Map

```csharp
using SharpImage;                  // ImagePipeline (fluent API)
using SharpImage.Image;            // ImageFrame, ImageSequence, PixelCache
using SharpImage.Core;             // Quantum, ColorspaceType, CompositeOperator,
                                   //   PixelChannel, FilterType, GravityType, enums
using SharpImage.Formats;          // FormatRegistry, JpegCoder, PngCoder, ...
                                   //   CameraRawCoder, TiffCompression,
                                   //   DemosaicAlgorithm, ImageFileFormat
using SharpImage.Transform;        // Resize, Geometry, Composite,
                                   //   InterpolationMethod, RotationAngle,
                                   //   CompositeMode, SeamCarving, SmartCrop
using SharpImage.Effects;          // ConvolutionFilters, BlurNoiseOps,
                                   //   ColorAdjust, ArtisticOps, NoiseType, ...
using SharpImage.Enhance;          // EnhanceOps
using SharpImage.Colorspaces;      // ColorspaceOps, ColorspaceConverter
using SharpImage.Channel;          // ChannelOps, AlphaOps
```

> **Note**: `ColorspaceType` lives in `SharpImage.Core`, NOT `SharpImage.Colorspaces`.

---

## Core Type: `ImageFrame`

The container for pixel data. `IDisposable` — always dispose (or use the pipeline).

Key properties (all on `ImageFrame`):

| Property | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Columns` | `long` | Width in pixels. **NOT `Width`.** |
| `Rows` | `long` | Height in pixels. **NOT `Height`.** |
| `NumberOfChannels` | `int` | 3 for RGB, 4 for RGBA, 1 for Gray |
| `HasAlpha` | `bool` | |
| `Colorspace` | `ColorspaceType` | Default `SRGB` |
| `Depth` | `int` | Default 16 (16-bit quantum) |
| `Quality` | `int` | Format-specific quality hint |
| `Metadata` | `ImageMetadata` | EXIF / XMP / ICC |

**Pixel values are 16-bit** (`ushort`, range 0–65535), not 0–255. Use
`Quantum.MaxValue` (= 65535) and `Quantum.Scale` (= 1/65535) when normalizing.

### Creating an `ImageFrame` from scratch

```csharp
using SharpImage.Core;
using SharpImage.Image;

var frame = new ImageFrame();
frame.Initialize(columns: 256, rows: 256,
                 colorspace: ColorspaceType.SRGB, hasAlpha: false);

// Write a row of red pixels
for (long y = 0; y < frame.Rows; y++)
{
    Span<ushort> row = frame.GetPixelRowForWrite(y);
    int channels = frame.NumberOfChannels;
    for (int x = 0; x < frame.Columns; x++)
    {
        int off = x * channels;
        row[off]     = Quantum.MaxValue;  // R
        row[off + 1] = 0;                 // G
        row[off + 2] = 0;                 // B
    }
}
```

### Pixel access

```csharp
// Read-only row
ReadOnlySpan<ushort> row = frame.GetPixelRow(y);

// Writable row
Span<ushort> writeRow = frame.GetPixelRowForWrite(y);

// Row length is Columns * NumberOfChannels, channel order is R, G, B[, A]

// Single-pixel access (slower than rows for bulk work)
ushort r = frame.GetPixelChannel(x, y, 0);
frame.SetPixelChannel(x, y, 0, (ushort)32768);
PixelInfo px = frame.GetPixel(x, y);
frame.SetPixel(x, y, in px);
```

### Cloning and disposing

```csharp
ImageFrame copy = frame.Clone();   // Independent copy
frame.Dispose();                   // Releases backing memory
```

---

## Loading and Saving

### Recommended: `FormatRegistry` (auto-detects format)

```csharp
using SharpImage.Formats;

// From file path — format detected from header bytes
ImageFrame img = FormatRegistry.Read("photo.jpg");

// From byte array
byte[] data = File.ReadAllBytes("photo.jpg");
ImageFrame img2 = FormatRegistry.Read(data);

// Write — format inferred from extension; quality applies to lossy formats
FormatRegistry.Write(img, "out.png");                   // PNG
FormatRegistry.Write(img, "out.jpg", quality: 90);      // JPEG
FormatRegistry.Write(img, "out.webp", quality: 80);     // WebP

// Round-trip through bytes
byte[] encoded = FormatRegistry.Encode(img, ImageFileFormat.Png);
ImageFrame decoded = FormatRegistry.Decode(encoded, ImageFileFormat.Png);
```

### Format-specific coders

Use these when you need format-specific options. Note that **not every coder
has a `string path` overload** — some are stream-only (e.g., `WebpCoder.Write`,
`BmpCoder.Write`).

```csharp
// JPEG — quality, subsampling, optional Huffman optimization
JpegCoder.Read("photo.jpg");                 // path or Stream
JpegCoder.Write(img, "out.jpg", quality: 85);
JpegCoder.WriteProgressive(img, "out.jpg", quality: 85);

// PNG — no quality knob; lossless
PngCoder.Read("photo.png");
PngCoder.Write(img, "out.png");

// PNG sequence (APNG) — returns a tuple
(ImageFrame[] Frames, int LoopCount, int[] DelaysMs) apng =
    PngCoder.ReadSequence("anim.apng");
PngCoder.WriteSequence(apng.Frames, "out.apng", apng.DelaysMs, loopCount: 0);

// GIF — animation returns ImageSequence (not a tuple)
ImageSequence gifAnim = GifCoder.ReadSequence("anim.gif");
GifCoder.WriteSequence(gifAnim, "out.gif");

// TIFF — compression options, multi-page
TiffCoder.Write(img, "out.tiff", TiffCompression.Deflate);  // None|Lzw|Deflate|PackBits
List<ImageFrame> pages = TiffCoder.ReadMultiPage("doc.tiff");
TiffCoder.WriteMultiPage(pages, "out.tiff", TiffCompression.Lzw);

// WebP — STREAM ONLY, no string-path overload
using (var fs = File.Create("out.webp"))
    WebpCoder.Write(img, fs, quality: 90);

// BMP — has both path and stream; bool for alpha channel
BmpCoder.Write(img, "out.bmp", includeAlpha: true);
```

### Available coders

| Class | Read | Write | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FormatRegistry` | ✅ | ✅ | Auto-detect; quality param on `Write` |
| `JpegCoder` | ✅ | ✅ | Quality, subsampling, progressive |
| `PngCoder` | ✅ | ✅ | Read/Write APNG sequences |
| `GifCoder` | ✅ | ✅ | Animation via `ImageSequence` |
| `TiffCoder` | ✅ | ✅ | Multi-page, tiled, compression options |
| `WebpCoder` | ✅ | ✅ | **Stream-only API** |
| `BmpCoder` | ✅ | ✅ | Optional alpha for 32-bit |
| `IcoCoder` | ✅ | ✅ | |
| `TgaCoder` | ✅ | ✅ | |
| `HeifCoder` | ✅ | ✅ | HEIC / AVIF |
| `JxlCoder` | ✅ | ✅ | JPEG XL |
| `Jpeg2000Coder` | ✅ | ✅ | |
| `ExrCoder` | ✅ | ✅ | OpenEXR |
| `HdrCoder` | ✅ | ✅ | Radiance HDR |
| `DpxCoder` / `CinCoder` | ✅ | ✅ | Film/cinema |
| `PsdCoder` | ✅ | ✅ | Photoshop |
| `DicomCoder` | ✅ | ✅ | Medical imaging |
| `FitsCoder` | ✅ | ✅ | Astronomy |
| `QoiCoder` | ✅ | ✅ | |
| `FarbfeldCoder`, `PnmCoder`, `WbmpCoder`, `XbmCoder`, `XpmCoder`, `SgiCoder`, `SunCoder`, `PixCoder`, `PcxCoder`, `DdsCoder` | ✅ | varies | Niche/legacy |
| `SvgCoder` | ✅ | rasterizes only | |
| `PdfCoder` | ✅ | rasterizes only | |
| `CameraRawCoder` | ✅ | DNG only | 31 raw formats |

---

## Common Recipes (Pipeline Style — Recommended)

### Resize and save

```csharp
using SharpImage;
using SharpImage.Transform;

using var p = ImagePipeline.Load("photo.jpg")
    .Resize(800, 600, InterpolationMethod.Lanczos3)
    .Save("resized.png");
```

### Thumbnail batch

```csharp
foreach (string path in Directory.GetFiles("photos", "*.jpg"))
{
    using var p = ImagePipeline.Load(path)
        .Resize(200, 200)            // for true aspect-fit thumbnail use Resize.Thumbnail
        .Sharpen(sigma: 0.5, amount: 1.0)
        .Save(Path.Combine("thumbs", Path.GetFileName(path)));
}
```

> For aspect-preserving thumbnails, use the static `Resize.Thumbnail(frame, maxW, maxH)`
> — the pipeline's `Resize` is a hard resize to exact dimensions.

### Crop, rotate, save as JPEG

```csharp
using var p = ImagePipeline.Load("portrait.png")
    .Crop(x: 100, y: 50, width: 800, height: 1200)
    .Rotate(RotationAngle.Rotate90)         // or .Rotate(45.0) for arbitrary angle
    .Save("portrait_cropped.jpg");
```

### Color-correct workflow

```csharp
using var p = ImagePipeline.Load("flat.jpg")
    .WhiteBalance()
    .AutoLevel()
    .Modulate(brightness: 105, saturation: 115, hue: 100)
    .Sharpen(sigma: 0.5, amount: 1.2)
    .Save("graded.jpg");
```

### Artistic

```csharp
using var p = ImagePipeline.Load("photo.jpg")
    .OilPaint(radius: 4)
    .Vignette(sigma: 30)
    .Save("painted.jpg");
```

### Apply an op the pipeline doesn't expose

```csharp
using SharpImage.Effects;

using var p = ImagePipeline.Load("photo.jpg")
    .Apply(frame => CreativeFilters.TiltShift(frame, /*params*/))
    .Save("tiltshift.jpg");
```

The `.Apply(Func<ImageFrame, ImageFrame>)` escape hatch lets you plug any
static op into a pipeline. The pipeline disposes the input frame and adopts
the returned one.

### Inspect mid-pipeline (read-only)

```csharp
using var p = ImagePipeline.Load("photo.jpg")
    .Resize(800, 600)
    .Inspect(f => Console.WriteLine($"After resize: {f.Columns}x{f.Rows}"))
    .GaussianBlur(2.0)
    .Save("out.png");
```

### Hand off the final frame instead of saving

```csharp
ImageFrame finalFrame = ImagePipeline.Load("in.jpg")
    .Resize(512, 512)
    .Grayscale()
    .ToFrame();         // pipeline releases ownership; you must dispose
// ... use finalFrame ...
finalFrame.Dispose();
```

### Encode to a byte array

```csharp
using var p = ImagePipeline.Load("in.jpg").Resize(256, 256);
byte[] pngBytes = p.Encode(ImageFileFormat.Png);
```

---

## Recipes (Static API)

Use these patterns when you're not in a pipeline — typically when you have
an existing `ImageFrame` you didn't load yourself.

### Resize

```csharp
using SharpImage.Transform;

using var src = FormatRegistry.Read("in.jpg");

// Hard resize to exact dimensions
using var resized = Resize.Apply(src, 800, 600, InterpolationMethod.Lanczos3);

// Aspect-preserving thumbnail (fits within bounds)
using var thumb = Resize.Thumbnail(src, maxWidth: 200, maxHeight: 200);

// Adaptive area-averaging downscale
using var adaptive = Resize.AdaptiveResize(src, 400, 300);

// Non-interpolated point sampling (pixel art / palette images)
using var sampled = Resize.Sample(src, 400, 300);
```

### Geometry

```csharp
using SharpImage.Transform;

using var cropped   = Geometry.Crop(src, x: 10, y: 10, width: 100, height: 100);
using var flipped   = Geometry.Flip(src);              // vertical
using var flopped   = Geometry.Flop(src);              // horizontal
using var rotated   = Geometry.Rotate(src, RotationAngle.Rotate90);   // 90/180/270
using var spun      = Geometry.RotateArbitrary(src, 37.5);            // any angle
using var trimmed   = Geometry.Trim(src, fuzz: 0.0);   // crop solid borders
using var transposed= Geometry.Transpose(src);         // diagonal flip
using var deskewed  = Geometry.Deskew(src, threshold: 0.4);
using var oriented  = Geometry.AutoOrient(src);        // honors EXIF orientation

// Resize the canvas without resizing the image
using var extended = Geometry.Extent(src, newWidth: 1000, newHeight: 800,
                                     xOffset: 50, yOffset: 50);

// Cut out an interior region
using var chopped = Geometry.Chop(src, chopX: 100, chopY: 100,
                                   chopWidth: 50, chopHeight: 50);
```

### Composite (overlay one image on another)

> **Important:** `Composite.Apply` returns `void` and **mutates `baseImage`
> in place**. This is the *only* mutating op in the public surface. Clone
> first if you need to keep the original.

```csharp
using SharpImage.Transform;

using var background = FormatRegistry.Read("bg.jpg");
using var logo       = FormatRegistry.Read("logo.png");

int x = (int)(background.Columns - logo.Columns) / 2;
int y = (int)(background.Rows - logo.Rows) / 2;

Composite.Apply(background, logo, offsetX: x, offsetY: y, mode: CompositeMode.Over);
//      ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ no return value — background is modified in place

FormatRegistry.Write(background, "result.jpg", quality: 95);
```

### Blur and sharpen

```csharp
using SharpImage.Effects;

using var blurred = ConvolutionFilters.GaussianBlur(src, sigma: 2.0);
using var sharp   = ConvolutionFilters.Sharpen(src, sigma: 1.0, amount: 2.0);
using var unsharp = ConvolutionFilters.UnsharpMask(src,
                        sigma: 1.0, amount: 1.5, threshold: 0.0);
using var edges   = ConvolutionFilters.EdgeDetect(src, radius: 1.0);
using var emboss  = ConvolutionFilters.Emboss(src);

// Motion blur lives on BlurNoiseOps, not ConvolutionFilters
using var motion  = BlurNoiseOps.MotionBlur(src,
                        radius: 5, sigma: 2.0, angle: 45.0);
using var radial  = BlurNoiseOps.RadialBlur(src, angle: 5.0);
using var noisy   = BlurNoiseOps.AddNoise(src, NoiseType.Gaussian, attenuate: 1.0);
using var denoised= BlurNoiseOps.WaveletDenoise(src, threshold: 0.05);
```

### Color adjustment

```csharp
using SharpImage.Effects;

using var brighter  = ColorAdjust.Brightness(src, factor: 1.2);  // >1 brighter
using var darker    = ColorAdjust.Brightness(src, factor: 0.8);  // <1 darker
using var contrast  = ColorAdjust.Contrast(src, factor: 1.3);
using var gamma     = ColorAdjust.Gamma(src, gamma: 0.8);
using var gray      = ColorAdjust.Grayscale(src);
using var inverted  = ColorAdjust.Invert(src);
using var posterize = ColorAdjust.Posterize(src, levels: 4);
using var saturated = ColorAdjust.Saturate(src, factor: 1.4);
using var thresholded = ColorAdjust.Threshold(src, threshold: 0.5);
using var levels    = ColorAdjust.Levels(src, /* see signature */);
using var exposed   = ColorAdjust.Exposure(src, evStops: 1.5);
using var vibrant   = ColorAdjust.Vibrance(src, amount: 0.4);
using var dehazed   = ColorAdjust.Dehaze(src, strength: 0.5, patchRadius: 7);
```

### Enhancement (auto-correction)

```csharp
using SharpImage.Enhance;

using var equalized = EnhanceOps.Equalize(src);                         // histogram eq
using var normalized= EnhanceOps.Normalize(src);                        // contrast stretch
using var leveled   = EnhanceOps.AutoLevel(src);
using var autoGamma = EnhanceOps.AutoGamma(src);
using var balanced  = EnhanceOps.WhiteBalance(src);

// Note: parameter is `contrast` (positional, no default), not `contrastLevel`
using var sigmoid   = EnhanceOps.SigmoidalContrast(src,
                          contrast: 5.0, midpoint: 0.5, sharpen: true);

// Note: separate tilesX, tilesY — not a single tileSize
using var clahe     = EnhanceOps.CLAHE(src,
                          tilesX: 8, tilesY: 8, clipLimit: 2.0);

using var modulated = EnhanceOps.Modulate(src,
                          brightness: 100, saturation: 100, hue: 100);
                      // values in % — 100 = no change

using var sepia     = EnhanceOps.SepiaTone(src, threshold: 0.8);
using var solar     = EnhanceOps.Solarize(src, threshold: 0.5);
using var tinted    = EnhanceOps.Colorize(src,
                          tintR: 200, tintG: 100, tintB: 50, amount: 0.5);
```

### Channel operations

```csharp
using SharpImage.Channel;

ImageFrame[] channels = ChannelOps.Separate(src);   // RGB → 3 grayscale frames
using var single = ChannelOps.SeparateChannel(src, channelIndex: 0);  // R only
using var combined = ChannelOps.Combine(channels);

// In-place channel swap (R↔B)
ChannelOps.SwapChannels(src, channel1: 0, channel2: 2);
```

### Alpha operations

```csharp
using SharpImage.Channel;
using SharpImage.Core;

using var alphaImg   = AlphaOps.Extract(rgbaSrc);              // alpha as gray image
using var noAlpha    = AlphaOps.Remove(rgbaSrc,                // composite onto bg
                          bgR: Quantum.MaxValue,
                          bgG: Quantum.MaxValue,
                          bgB: Quantum.MaxValue);
using var withAlpha  = AlphaOps.SetAlpha(rgbSrc, alphaValue: Quantum.MaxValue);
using var opaque     = AlphaOps.MakeOpaque(rgbaSrc);
using var keyed      = AlphaOps.MakeTransparent(src,
                          targetR: 0, targetG: Quantum.MaxValue, targetB: 0,
                          fuzz: 0.05);
```

### Colorspace conversion

> **Important:** `ColorspaceOps` takes lowercase **strings**, not the
> `ColorspaceType` enum. The set of strings is a *subset* of the enum values.
> See `ColorspaceOps.SupportedColorspaces` for the authoritative list.

Supported strings: `"hsl"`, `"hsv"`, `"hsi"`, `"hwb"`, `"hcl"`, `"hclp"`,
`"xyz"`, `"lab"`, `"lchab"`, `"luv"`, `"lchuv"`, `"lms"`, `"ypbpr"`,
`"ycbcr"`, `"yiq"`, `"yuv"`, `"ydbdr"`, `"oklab"`, `"oklch"`, `"jzazbz"`,
`"jzczhz"`, `"displayp3"`, `"prophoto"`.

```csharp
using SharpImage.Colorspaces;

using var inLab     = ColorspaceOps.ConvertToColorspace(src, "lab");
using var backToRgb = ColorspaceOps.ConvertFromColorspace(inLab, "lab");
using var roundTrip = ColorspaceOps.RoundTrip(src, "oklab");

IReadOnlyList<string> all = ColorspaceOps.SupportedColorspaces;

// Per-pixel direct conversion (inputs are quantum-scale doubles, 0..65535)
ColorspaceConverter.RgbToHsl(red: 65535.0, green: 32768.0, blue: 16384.0,
                             out double h, out double s, out double l);
ColorspaceConverter.RgbToLab(65535.0, 32768.0, 16384.0,
                             out double L, out double a, out double b);
```

> **Pixel-input range gotcha:** the per-pixel `ColorspaceConverter.RgbTo*`
> methods take *quantum-scale* doubles (0–65535), not 0–255. Multiply byte
> inputs by 257 (or use `Quantum.ScaleFromByte`) before passing them in.

### Camera Raw

```csharp
using SharpImage.Formats;

byte[] rawBytes = File.ReadAllBytes("DSC_0001.nef");

// Metadata-only — fast, no decode
CameraRawMetadata meta = CameraRawCoder.GetMetadata(rawBytes);
Console.WriteLine($"{meta.Make} {meta.Model}");
Console.WriteLine($"Sensor: {meta.SensorWidth}x{meta.SensorHeight}, " +
                  $"image area: {meta.ActiveAreaWidth}x{meta.ActiveAreaHeight}");
Console.WriteLine($"ISO {meta.IsoSpeed}, f/{meta.FNumber}, {meta.ExposureTime}s, " +
                  $"{meta.FocalLength}mm");
//                ^^^ NOTE: IsoSpeed (not Iso), FNumber (not Aperture),
//                          ExposureTime (not ShutterSpeed)

// Full decode — defaults to AHD demosaicing, 16-bit, gamma applied
var opts = new CameraRawDecodeOptions
{
    Algorithm = DemosaicAlgorithm.AHD,        // Bilinear | VNG | AHD
    WhiteBalance = WhiteBalanceMode.AsShot,
    OutputBitDepth = 16,
    ApplyColorMatrix = true,
    ApplyGamma = true,
    HighlightRecovery = 0,
};
using var raw = CameraRawCoder.Decode(rawBytes, opts);

// Or use Default
using var rawDefault = CameraRawCoder.Decode(rawBytes, CameraRawDecodeOptions.Default);

// DNG is the only raw format that supports encoding
byte[] dng = CameraRawCoder.Encode(raw);
```

Supported raw formats: CR2, CR3, CRW, NEF, NRW, ARW, SR2, SRF, DNG, ORF, RW2,
RAF, PEF, SRW, 3FR, IIQ, X3F, DCR, K25, KDC, MDC, MEF, MOS, MRW, RMF, RWL,
ERF, FFF, STI.

---

## Enums Reference

### `InterpolationMethod` (in `SharpImage.Transform`)

```
NearestNeighbor, Bilinear, Bicubic, Lanczos3 (default), Triangle, Hermite,
Mitchell, Catrom, Gaussian, Sinc, Hann, Hamming, Blackman, Kaiser,
Lanczos2, Lanczos4, Lanczos5, Spline, Parzen, Bohman, Bartlett, Welch, Lagrange
```

Recommendation: `Lanczos3` for general-purpose resizing (the default).
`NearestNeighbor` for pixel art. `Bilinear` for fastest non-degenerate.

### `CompositeMode` (in `SharpImage.Transform`)

```
Over (default), Multiply, Screen, Overlay, Add, Subtract, Replace,
Darken, Lighten, ColorDodge, ColorBurn, HardLight, SoftLight,
Difference, Exclusion, Dissolve, Atop, In, Out, Xor, Plus, Minus,
ModulusAdd, ModulusSubtract, Bumpmap, HardMix, LinearLight,
VividLight, PinLight
```

### `RotationAngle` (in `SharpImage.Transform`)

```
Rotate90 = 90, Rotate180 = 180, Rotate270 = 270
```

For other angles use `Geometry.RotateArbitrary(src, double angleDegrees)`.

### `ColorspaceType` (in `SharpImage.Core`)

Note these are PascalCase, including `SRGB` (not `sRGB`), `Adobe98`, `Oklab`,
`Oklch`, `XyY`. This enum is used on `ImageFrame.Colorspace`. It does NOT
overlap exactly with the strings accepted by `ColorspaceOps`.

```
Undefined, CMY, CMYK, Gray, HCL, HCLp, HSB, HSI, HSL, HSV, HWB, Lab, LCH,
LCHab, LCHuv, Log, LMS, Luv, OHTA, Rec601YCbCr, Rec709YCbCr, RGB, ScRGB,
SRGB, Transparent, XyY, XYZ, YCbCr, YCC, YDbDr, YIQ, YPbPr, YUV,
LinearGray, Jzazbz, DisplayP3, Adobe98, ProPhoto, Oklab, Oklch, CAT02LMS
```

### `TiffCompression` (in `SharpImage.Formats`)

```
None = 1, Lzw = 5, Deflate = 8, PackBits = 32773
```

Note PascalCase: `Lzw`, not `LZW`.

### `DemosaicAlgorithm` (in `SharpImage.Formats`)

```
Bilinear, VNG, AHD (default)
```

### `NoiseType` (in `SharpImage.Effects`)

Used by `BlurNoiseOps.AddNoise`. Common values: `Gaussian`, `Uniform`,
`Impulse`, `Laplacian`, `Poisson`, `Random`, `Multiplicative`. (Verify the
exact set in `BlurNoiseOps.cs` before relying on rare ones.)

---

## Threading and Async

- **Internal parallelism is automatic.** Most heavy ops (`Resize`, `Composite`,
  `ConvolutionFilters.*`, `BlurNoiseOps.*`, `ColorspaceOps.*`) use
  `Parallel.For` internally over scanlines. You do not need to thread
  these yourself.

- **A single `ImageFrame` is NOT safe for concurrent writes.** Treat it as
  you would a mutable collection: one writer at a time, or one writer + no
  readers. Read-only concurrent access (multiple `GetPixelRow` calls from
  different threads) is fine as long as nothing is calling
  `GetPixelRowForWrite` concurrently.

- **Static op classes are stateless and thread-safe.** You can call
  `Resize.Apply(srcA, …)` and `Resize.Apply(srcB, …)` from different threads
  on different sources at the same time.

- **Batch processing pattern** — fan out across files with `Parallel.ForEach`,
  one frame per task:

  ```csharp
  Parallel.ForEach(Directory.GetFiles("photos", "*.jpg"), path =>
  {
      using var p = ImagePipeline.Load(path)
          .Resize(1920, 1080)
          .Save(Path.Combine("out", Path.GetFileName(path)));
  });
  ```

- **No async APIs.** All I/O is synchronous. If you need async, wrap the
  whole pipeline in `Task.Run`:

  ```csharp
  byte[] result = await Task.Run(() =>
  {
      using var p = ImagePipeline.Load("in.jpg").Resize(800, 600);
      return p.Encode(ImageFileFormat.Png);
  });
  ```

---

## Exceptions

What you can expect to be thrown:

- **`ArgumentOutOfRangeException`** — invalid dimensions (zero/negative width
  or height), out-of-bounds pixel access.
- **`ArgumentException`** — unsupported colorspace string, malformed
  arguments, missing required content (e.g., empty frame list).
- **`InvalidDataException`** — corrupt or malformed image data (bad PNG
  chunks, missing JPEG markers, truncated files, unknown variants within
  a known format).
- **`EndOfStreamException`** — file ended before the format expected.
- **`NotSupportedException`** — operation valid but not implemented for the
  given format (e.g., multi-frame write to a format that doesn't support it).
- **`ObjectDisposedException`** — using an `ImagePipeline` or `ImageFrame`
  after `Dispose`.
- **`InvalidOperationException`** — pipeline misuse (e.g., reusing a
  pipeline whose frame was extracted via `ToFrame()`).

There is no SharpImage-specific exception type. Catch the BCL exceptions above
or `Exception` for a top-level guard around format I/O.

---

## Anti-patterns (Don'ts)

These prevent specific common mistakes:

1. **Don't write `frame.Width` or `frame.Height`.** They are `Columns` and
   `Rows`, both `long`. Use `(int)frame.Columns` if you need an `int`.

2. **Don't compare pixel values to 255.** Pixel storage is 16-bit (0–65535).
   `row[off] > 128` does NOT mean "above mid-gray." Use `Quantum.MaxValue / 2`
   or `row[off] * Quantum.Scale > 0.5`.

3. **Don't assume `Composite.Apply` returns a new frame.** It mutates the
   base in place and returns `void`. Clone the base first if you need to
   keep the original.

4. **Don't pass `ColorspaceType` to `ColorspaceOps`.** It takes a lowercase
   string. `ColorspaceOps.ConvertToColorspace(frame, ColorspaceType.Lab)`
   is a compile error.

5. **Don't dispose a frame you've passed to `ImagePipeline.Wrap`.** `Wrap`
   takes ownership; the pipeline disposes it. Use `From` if you want to
   keep your own copy (it clones).

6. **Don't dispose the frame returned by `pipeline.ToFrame()` and then
   continue using the pipeline.** `ToFrame` releases ownership; the pipeline
   becomes unusable afterward.

7. **Don't write manual pixel loops to do work an op already does.** A
   for-loop over `GetPixelRowForWrite` to scale brightness will be 5–50×
   slower than `ColorAdjust.Brightness` (which is SIMD-accelerated and
   parallelized).

8. **Don't call `Dispose()` twice on the same frame.** Idempotent in
   current builds but not contractually guaranteed.

9. **Don't try to re-use an `ImageFrame` after it has been the input to a
   pipeline `.Wrap()` or `.From(...).Save().Dispose()`.** Once the pipeline
   disposes it, the backing memory is gone.

10. **Don't pass byte values (0–255) to `ColorspaceConverter.RgbTo*`** — they
    take quantum-scale doubles (0–65535). Use `Quantum.ScaleFromByte(b)` to
    convert first, or pass `byteVal * 257.0`.

---

## Performance Notes

- **All heavy ops are SIMD + parallelized internally.** No need to add
  `Parallel.For` around them.
- **Pixel storage is 16-bit per channel** — both quality (matches ImageMagick)
  and SIMD-friendly. Don't try to "optimize" by truncating to 8-bit yourself.
- **Operations return new frames.** The only mutating op in the public
  surface is `Composite.Apply`. If you need to chain many ops on a hot path,
  prefer `ImagePipeline` so intermediate disposals happen automatically and
  cheaply via `ArrayPool<T>`.
- **`Resize.Apply` complexity scales with output size and kernel radius.**
  Lanczos3 is ~3× the work of Bilinear at the same resolution but produces
  visibly better results for downscale.
- **Large images** (above available memory) are automatically backed by
  disk via `PixelCache` — you don't need to do anything special, but
  expect operations to be IO-bound.

---

## Summary for Agents

When generating SharpImage code:

1. **Reach for `ImagePipeline.Load(...).…Save(...)` first.** It's terser
   and disposal-safe. Drop to static classes only when you need an op the
   pipeline doesn't expose.
2. **Always `using` or `Dispose()` everything that came out of `Read`,
   `Apply`, `Crop`, `Resize`, etc.** These are all `IDisposable`.
3. **Use `Columns` and `Rows`** (`long`), not `Width`/`Height`.
4. **Pixels are `ushort` 0–65535.** Use `Quantum.MaxValue` and `Quantum.Scale`.
5. **`Composite.Apply` mutates the base.** No assignment, returns `void`.
6. **`ColorspaceOps` takes strings.** `ColorspaceType` enum is for the
   `ImageFrame.Colorspace` property, not for `ColorspaceOps` calls.
7. **No async APIs.** Wrap in `Task.Run` if needed.
8. **No SharpImage-specific exceptions.** Catch BCL types or `Exception`.
